# API performance (generated by scripts/benchmark_api.py)

Machine: Intel64 Family 6 Model 94 Stepping 3, GenuineIntel, 2 logical CPUs, 8.5 GB RAM; uvicorn, 1 worker, CPU only; Python 3.12.9. These are single-machine, single-worker figures measured on a quiet laptop, not production capacity. Requests are sequential unless stated; 30 repetitions after one warm-up.

Server start to healthy: 7.24 s. Memory (resident): 191 MB idle, 227 MB after building two fleets, 247 MB after the load test. Bundle load from disk (in process): 0.09 s.

## First calls (cold)

| Request | ms |
|---|---|
| GET /fleet/FD001 (first call, computes every engine) | 1,374 |
| GET /fleet/FD004 (first call, computes every engine) | 3,245 |

## Warm sequential requests

| Request | p50 ms | p95 ms | max ms |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET /health | 14.0 | 16.1 | 17.4 |
| GET /subsets | 14.5 | 15.3 | 15.6 |
| GET /fleet/FD001 (cached, 25 rows) | 5.8 | 9.9 | 13.6 |
| GET /engines/FD001/34 (203 cycles) | 73.2 | 104.9 | 128.4 |
| GET /replay cycle 10 | 42.6 | 44.8 | 47.0 |
| GET /replay cycle 100 | 55.4 | 58.3 | 80.3 |
| GET /replay cycle 200 | 71.2 | 76.7 | 100.0 |
| GET /explain cycle 200 | 37.9 | 63.4 | 198.4 |
| GET /evaluation/FD001 | 23.2 | 24.1 | 25.1 |
| GET /models | 25.0 | 27.6 | 51.8 |
| POST /predict/rul 50 rows | 41.2 | 43.5 | 43.8 |
| POST /predict/rul 200 rows | 46.4 | 51.5 | 78.4 |
| POST /predict/rul 1000 rows (tiled stress input) | 75.9 | 84.7 | 99.5 |
| POST /predict/rul 3000 rows (tiled stress input, API maximum) | 157.0 | 165.6 | 181.1 |

## Concurrent (8 clients, 25 requests each)

| Request | throughput req/s | p50 ms | p95 ms | max ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET /replay cycle 100 | 21.3 | 367.8 | 481.1 | 522.6 |
| POST /predict/rul 200 rows | 21.2 | 373.4 | 463.5 | 495.2 |

## Model alone (no HTTP), whole-history prediction for every cycle

| Call | p50 ms | p95 ms |
|---|---|---|
| predict_history, 50 rows | 36.9 | 38.9 |
| predict_history, 200 rows | 58.1 | 213.8 |
| predict_history, 1000 rows | 167.5 | 194.1 |

Notes: replay recomputes the model on the visible history at every step (so the server provably never sees later cycles); its cost grows with the cycle number. The 1000 and 3000 row inputs are real engine history tiled with re-indexed time, used only to stress the endpoint.
